title: Charge a low-battery robot long enough to reach a level that allows it to start and be added back into the system
summary: Recover a low-battery robot by charging it for a short period so it reaches a battery level sufficient to start and be added back into the system. The source provides example timing/levels: ~10 minutes to get enough juice to start, and charging from ~25% for ~15 minutes may bring the robot to ~40%, described as “good enough for the system” to cycle on its own.
when_to_use: Use when a robot is at a low battery level and needs a short charge to reach a level that allows it to start and be re-entered into the system so it can cycle on its own.
not_for: Do not use if the robot cannot reach the source-indicated sufficient battery level after the short charging period; escalate instead.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Execute the low-battery recovery by placing the robot on an appropriate charger, monitoring battery percentage, and re-adding the robot to the system once the battery level is sufficient.
safety_notes: The source indicates that at very low battery levels the robot may not accept new tasks and may turn off automatically (example thresholds mentioned: under 20% and at 15%). Avoid operating/attempting to start the robot when it is near these low thresholds; use the charger-based recovery approach.
access_or_tools_needed: Access to robot battery percentage display
Ability to place the robot on a charger and manage charging availability

access_required: Access to the live system view that shows the robot battery percentage
system_preconditions: A charger is available for the robot to charge

visual_references.description: Charger selection/charging guidance and example battery thresholds/timing (e.g., under 20% not accept new task; 15% turns off; 25% for 15 minutes to ~40%; ensure charger is turned back on).

steps.title: Identify the robot’s current battery percentage
steps.purpose: Determine whether the robot is in a low-battery range that requires short charging to reach a level sufficient to start and re-enter the system.
steps.instruction: Check the robot’s current battery percentage in the live system view you are using for robot status.
steps.expected_result: A current battery percentage value is identified for the robot (examples discussed in the source include ~25%, ~30%, and ~40%).
steps.healthy_condition: Battery percentage is clearly visible and corresponds to a low-battery scenario where charging is appropriate (e.g., around the ~25% example discussed).
steps.failure_condition: Battery percentage is not visible/unknown, or the value is so low that the robot may not accept new tasks or may turn off automatically (source examples: under 20% / at 15%).

actions.label: Read battery percentage
actions.exact_action: Identify the robot’s current battery percentage

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Nearby transcript: 'it only takes what, maybe 10 minutes to get enough juice to be able to start... If you’re 25%, you charge for 15 minutes, you’re probably gonna be at 40%, which is good enough for the system... to cycle it on its own.'
Source also states: 'under 20% it, it will not accept any new task' and 'at 15% it will, it will turn off automatically.'

steps.title: Place the robot on a charger and charge for the short period
steps.purpose: Provide enough charge for the robot to start and be cycled back into the system after a short charging period.
steps.instruction: Place the robot on a charger and allow charging for the short period described by the source examples (e.g., ~15 minutes when starting around ~25%). Ensure the charger is enabled/available for charging after any charger selection/disablement you perform.
steps.expected_result: The robot has been charged for the source-indicated short period (example: 15 minutes from ~25%).
steps.healthy_condition: Charging proceeds without the robot being left in a state where it cannot accept new tasks (source example: under 20% not accept new task) or turns off automatically (source example: at 15%).
steps.failure_condition: Charging cannot be performed (no charger available), or the charger is left disabled/off such that the robot cannot charge as intended.

actions.label: Charge robot on charger
actions.exact_action: Place the robot on a charger and allow charging for the source-indicated short period (example: charge for 15 minutes from ~25%)

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Nearby transcript: 'it only takes what, maybe 10 minutes to get enough juice to be able to start... If you’re 25%, you charge for 15 minutes, you’re probably gonna be at 40%...'
Source guidance on charger selection/availability: 'If you need to use a charger to manually charge a robot you can disable a charger... Once we take it off, we turn the charger back on.'

steps.title: Verify battery percentage increased to a sufficient level
steps.purpose: Confirm the robot reached the battery level described as sufficient for system use so it can start/cycle on its own.
steps.instruction: After the short charging period, re-check the robot’s battery percentage and confirm it increased to the source-indicated sufficient level (example: ~40% described as 'good enough for the system').
steps.expected_result: Battery percentage is at/near the source-indicated sufficient level (example: ~40% after charging from ~25% for ~15 minutes).
steps.healthy_condition: Battery percentage is high enough that the robot can start and be cycled back into the system (source example: ~40% is 'good enough for the system').
steps.failure_condition: Battery percentage does not reach the source-indicated sufficient level after the short charging period.

actions.label: Re-check battery percentage
actions.exact_action: Verify the battery percentage has increased to a level described as sufficient for the system (example: ~40% is 'good enough for the system')

stop_or_escalate_if: Robot does not reach the source-indicated sufficient battery level after the short charging period

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Nearby transcript: 'If you’re 25%, you charge for 15 minutes, you’re probably gonna be at 40%, which is good enough for the system... to cycle it on its own.'
Source also states: 'it only takes what, maybe 10 minutes to get enough juice to be able to start...'

steps.title: Add the robot back into the system so it can start/cycle on its own
steps.purpose: Return the robot to normal system operation after it has enough charge to start and cycle.
steps.instruction: Once the battery percentage is sufficient, add the robot back into the system so it can start/cycle on its own (source wording: 'add it back in the system' and 'to cycle it on its own').
steps.expected_result: The robot is added back into the system and is able to cycle on its own after the short charging period.
steps.healthy_condition: Robot transitions from low-battery recovery back into normal operation (source example: ~40% is 'good enough for the system' to cycle on its own).
steps.failure_condition: After re-adding, the robot does not start/cycle as expected (e.g., because it did not reach the sufficient battery level).

actions.label: Add robot back to system
actions.exact_action: Add the robot back into the system so it can start/cycle on its own

stop_or_escalate_if: If the robot does not reach the source-indicated sufficient battery level after the short charging period, stop and escalate to support.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Nearby transcript: '...add it back in the system... If you’re 25%, you charge for 15 minutes, you’re probably gonna be at 40%, which is good enough for the system... to cycle it on its own.'

success_criteria: Robot reaches the source-indicated sufficient battery level after a short charging period (example: ~40% after 25% + 15 minutes) and can be added back into the system to cycle on its own.
healthy_conditions: Battery percentage increases from the low starting point to the source-indicated sufficient level (example: ~40%).
Robot can start and cycle after being added back into the system.
failure_conditions: Robot does not reach the source-indicated sufficient battery level after the short charging period.
Robot is at/near very low thresholds where it may not accept new tasks (source example: under 20%) or may turn off automatically (source example: at 15%).
escalation_guidance: If the robot does not reach the source-indicated sufficient battery level after the short charging period, stop and escalate to support.
